claims.text: Adding 2–3 vol% nano-SiC and using spark plasma sintering at approximately 1700 °C will enable lower-temperature densification of ZrB2.
Sintering at approximately 1700 °C and 50 MPa in an inert atmosphere for about 10 minutes will produce rapid densification.
The added nano-SiC will be well dispersed in the ZrB2 body.
High-temperature exposure will cause the nano-SiC to form a continuous SiO2 layer along ZrB2 grain boundaries.
Nano-SiC facilitates a transient liquid-phase sintering mechanism in ZrB2.
The proposed transient liquid phase accelerates ZrB2 densification at lower temperatures.
A nano-SiC-derived SiO2 layer will impede oxygen ingress.
A nano-SiC-derived SiO2 layer will impede penetration by liquid plating metals.
The proposed composite will have greater oxidation durability than single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed composite will have greater resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion than single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed composite will have improved mechanical strength relative to single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The ZrB2–nano-SiC composite will reach full densification at approximately 1700 °C.
The proposed process will produce a refined microstructure.
Traditional single-phase ZrB2 requires processing temperatures above 2300 °C.
Earlier lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens typically have inferior oxidation resistance.
Earlier lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens are vulnerable to liquid-metal corrosion.
The proposed benefits are expected during oxidizing service above approximately 1000 °C.
